description: Publish a plugin to the plugin library: a new entry, or a new version of the entry the plugin already has. Publishing makes the plugin's agents, skills, MCP servers, files and rules visible to every signed-in Athenode user and turns the entry's public display on, unless an administrator made public display unavailable for the entry. Public display shows the entry's name, description and category and the full content of its agents, skills with their bundle files, rules and plugin files on the open web, without an account, where search engines can index them. Its MCP server configuration is public too: anyone can install the entry, MCP servers included, without an account with `npx @athenode/cli use <slug>`, so MCP values must stay ${VAR} references. After it is turned off, the entry can stay on the public site for up to a day and longer in search engines' caches. So publishing needs the explicit `confirmPublic: true`, the one consent to both; ask the user before setting it, naming the open web, and there is no `publicDisplay` here (to turn public display off afterwards use library_edit). Without `confirmPublic: true` nothing is published: the result is `{published: false, preview, problem}` with a warning, and a second one when an administrator excluded the entry from the public site (`publicDisplayBanned: true`: it is then published to the in-app library only; tell the user before confirming); the preview lists the items as `{id, name}` / `{id, path}` objects, and `problem` (`{status, code, field, error}`, else `null`) is the first refusal the publish would get: an invalid name, description, note or category, a first publish without a category (`library_entry_category_required`), or a name another entry has (`library_entry_name_taken`), which a confirmed publish answers as an error. A first publish beyond the plan's library entry limit (3 entries on the Free plan) is such a refusal too: `problem` in the preview, an error when confirmed (402 `plan_limit_exceeded`, limit `libraryEntries`); new versions of an existing entry are not limited. The entry and the preview carry `publicDisplay` and `publicDisplayBanned` as stored, `null` in the preview of a plugin with no entry yet. Refused in both modes: a plan that cannot publish and MCP servers holding literal `env`/`headers` values, plugin-level or inline in an agent's metadata (code `mcp_literal_secrets`, with the `servers` and keys to turn into `${VAR}` references; an inline server names its `agent`). Nothing is regenerated locally. `plugin` is required and is the plugin's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `pluginById: true` (see plugins_list); the installed plugin is never assumed.

category.description: The entry's category (CLI: --category): required for a new entry, kept by a new version when omitted. One of: programming, testing-qa, security, devops, design, productivity, other.

confirmPublic.description: Confirms what becomes visible, public display included (CLI: --confirm-public). Required to publish. Publishing makes the plugin's agents, skills, MCP servers, files and rules visible to every signed-in Athenode user and turns the entry's public display on, unless an administrator made public display unavailable for the entry. Public display shows the entry's name, description and category and the full content of its agents, skills with their bundle files, rules and plugin files on the open web, without an account, where search engines can index them. Its MCP server configuration is public too: anyone can install the entry, MCP servers included, without an account with `npx @athenode/cli use <slug>`, so MCP values must stay ${VAR} references. After it is turned off, the entry can stay on the public site for up to a day and longer in search engines' caches.

name.description: The entry's name; the plugin's name (or the entry's current one) if omitted.

note.description: A note for the published version.

plugin.description: Name of the plugin to act on, or its id with pluginById (CLI: --plugin). Required.

pluginById.description: `plugin` is a plugin id, not a name (CLI: --plugin-by-id).
